{{Short description|Mathematical theory of knots}}
In the [[knot theory|mathematical theory of knots]], the '''Thurston–Bennequin number''', or '''Bennequin number''', is an invariant associated with a [[Legendrian knot]] in a three dimensional [[contact manifold]]. It is named after [[William Thurston]] and [[Daniel Bennequin]]. The Thurston-Bennequin number measures the "twisting of the contact structure around the knot".<ref name="Bennequin"/> Together with the [[rotation number]], they are often referred as the "classical" invariants of [[Legendrian knots]].

The Thurston-Bennequin number of a Legendrian knot <math>K</math> is usually denoted by <math>\mathrm{tb}(K)</math>. The '''maximal Thurston–Bennequin number''', <math>\overline{\mathrm{tb}}(K)</math>, over all Legendrian representatives of a knot in <math> \mathbb R^3 </math> is a topological [[knot invariant]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ng |first=Lenhard |date=2012 |title=On arc index and maximal thurston–bennequin number |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/S0218216511009820 |journal=Journal of Knot Theory and Its Ramifications |volume=21 |issue=04 |pages=1250031 |doi=10.1142/S0218216511009820 |issn=0218-2165|arxiv=math/0612356 }}</ref>

==Definition and properties==

Let <math>K</math> be a null-homologous oriented [[Legendrian knot]] in a co-oriented three-dimensional [[contact manifold]] <math>(M^3,\xi)</math> and fix a [[Seifert surface]] <math>\Sigma</math> to <math>K</math>, that is an embedded connected, compact, orientable surface with boundary <math>\partial \Sigma = K</math>. The Thurston-Bennequin number of <math>K</math> relative to <math>\Sigma</math> is the defined as the signed [[intersection number]] of the contact plane field <math>\xi</math> with <math>\Sigma</math>.<ref name="Geiges' book">{{cite book
|title= An introduction to contact topology; Volume 109 of Cambridge studies in advanced mathematics
|last=Geiges 
|first=Hansjörg
|authorlink=Hansjörg Geiges 
|year=2008 
|publisher=Cambridge University Press 
|location= 
|isbn=978-0-521-86585-2 
|page=94 
|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RERR4zMDYRgC&dq=%22Legendrian+knot%22&pg=PA94 }}</ref>

Let <math>K'</math> be a small push-off of <math>K</math> obtained by pushing along a vector field <math>v</math> transverse to <math>\xi</math>. The Thurston-Bennequin number can also be defined as <math>\mathrm{lk}(K,K')</math>, where <math>\mathrm{lk}</math> denotes the [[linking number]].<ref name="Geiges' book/>

===The Euclidean case===

We consider the case where <math>(M,\xi)=(\mathbb{R}^3,\xi_{\mathrm{std}})</math> is [[Contact geometry#The standard contact structure|the standard contact structure]] on <math>\mathbb{R}^3</math>. If we denote <math>(x,y,z)</math> the coordinates in <math>\mathbb{R}^3</math>, the contact structure <math>\xi_{\mathrm{std}}</math> is the kernel of the one-form <math>dz-ydx</math>. The applications <math>\Pi \colon \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^2, (x,y,z) \mapsto (x,z)</math> and <math> \pi_L \colon \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^2, (x,y,z) \mapsto (x,y)</math> denote respectively the '''front projection''' and the '''Lagrangian projection'''. The Thurston-Bennequin number can be computed easily from its front and Lagrangian projections.

====Lagrangian projection description====

The Thurston-Bennequin number of a Legendrian knot <math>K \subset \mathbb R^3</math> is the [[writhe]] of its Lagrangian projection <math> \pi_L(K) </math>.

====Front projection description====

For a Legendrian knot <math> K \subset \mathbb{R}^3</math>, its front projection <math>\Pi(K)\subset \mathbb R^2</math> is called its '''front diagram'''. The front diagram of a Legendrian knot does not have vertical tangencies, however [[Cusp (singularity)|cusps]] can appear. Generically, the front diagram of a knot as no [[tangency]] point, no triple intersection and standard [[Cusp (singularity)|cusp]] singularities. In this case the Thurston-Bennequin number is
:<math>\mathrm{tb}(K)=\textrm{writhe}(\Pi(K))-\dfrac{1}{2}\big(\# \text{number of cusps}\big),</math>
where <math>\textrm{writhe}(\Pi(K))</math> denotes the [[writhe]] of the front diagram.<ref name="Bennequin">{{cite journal|title=Entrelacements et équations de Pfaff|journal=Astérisque|volume=107/108|year=1983|pages=87–161}} (Bennequin's doctoral dissertation)</ref>

The invariant can also be computed using a '''grid diagram''' corresponding to a particular Legendrian representative of a knot.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Ozsváth |first=Peter S. |title=Grid Homology for Knots and Links |last2=Stipsicz |first2=András I. |last3=Szabó |first3=Zoltán |publisher=American Mathematical Society |year=2015 |isbn=978-1-4704-3442-7 |pages=220–221}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dynnikov |first=I. |last2=Prasolov |first2=M. |date=2013 |title=Bypasses for rectangular diagrams. A proof of the Jones conjecture and related questions |url=https://www.ams.org/mosc/2013-74-00/S0077-1554-2014-00210-7/ |journal=Transactions of the Moscow Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=74 |pages=97–144 |doi=10.1090/S0077-1554-2014-00210-7 |issn=0077-1554|arxiv=1206.0898 }}</ref> In this setting, the number can be computed as the writhe of the diagram minus the number of 'northwest' corners. 
[[File:Grid-diagram-to-Legendrian-conversion.svg|center|thumb|801x801px|A grid diagram of the knot <math>8_{20}</math> and an associated Legendrian representative of it.]]
By smoothing the 'northeast' and 'southwest' corners and rotating the diagram and switching all crossings, one can convert a grid diagram into the associated Legendrian knot.

==The Bennequin inequality==

In his thesis <ref name="Bennequin"/>, [[Daniel Bennequin]] proved an inequality involving the Thurston-Bennequin number. He proved that for all Legendrian knot <math>K</math> in [[Contact geometry#The standard contact structure|the standard contact]] <math> \mathbb R^3</math> the following inequality is true:
:<math> \mathrm{tb}(K)+\vert \textrm{rot}(K) \vert \leq - \chi(\Sigma),</math>
where <math>\chi(\Sigma)</math> denotes the [[Euler characteristic]] of a [[Seifert surface]] <math>\Sigma</math> of <math> K </math> and <math> \textrm{rot}(K)</math> denotes the [[rotation number]] of <math> K </math>. 

In particular, the '''maximal Thurston-Bennequin number''' gives a lower bound on the [[Seifert surface #Genus of a knot| genus]] of a topological knot.
